# New renderings — odyssey-086 (17.409–507)

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| τὸν δ’ ἀναχωρήσας προσέφη πολύμητις Ὀδυσσεύς (whole-line reply-formula, 17.453; participle added to the table's τὸν δ’ ἄρ’ ὑπόδρα ἰδὼν προσέφη πολύμητις Ὀδυσσεύς) | "Him then, drawing back, addressed many-wiled Odysseus:" | "Then Odysseus of many wiles, stepping back, spoke to him:" | "answered" (reserved for ἠμείβετο), "retreating", "withdrawing" (too military); built on the table's πολύμητις and προσέφη rows |
| τὴν δ’ αὖτ’ Εὐρυνόμη ταμίη πρὸς μῦθον ἔειπεν (whole-line reply-formula, 17.495; name + ταμίη + πρὸς … ἔειπεν) | "Her then in turn Eurynome, the housekeeper, with a word addressed:" | "Then the housekeeper Eurynome spoke to her in turn:" | "answered" (reserved for ἠμείβετο); follows the table's τὸν καὶ Πείραιος πρότερος πρὸς μῦθον ἔειπε "with a word addressed", and ταμίη keeps "housekeeper" |
| κλυτότοξος Ἀπόλλων (17.494) | "famed-for-the-bow Apollo" | "Apollo, famed for his bow" | "far-famed archer" (loses τόξον), "renowned bowman", "bow-famous"; built on the table's δουρικλειτὸς Μενέλαος "famed-for-the-spear" / "famed for his spear" and κλυτός "famous" |
| μαῖα (vocative μαῖ’, of the housekeeper Eurynome, 17.499; shipped at 2.349 and 2.372 as "Nurse" of Eurycleia) | "Good mother" | "Good mother" | "Nurse" here (Eurynome is not a nurse; the word is an address to an older woman, and a nurse only by context); "Mother" alone, "Old dame" |
| προΐκτης (17.449, ἐσσι προΐκτης; the shipped 17.352 has "beggar" for ἀνδρὶ προΐκτῃ) | "beggar" | "beggar" | "mendicant", "one who asks for gifts" (a gloss, not a rendering); the same English as πτωχός, the two words told apart by context |
| ἄχος beside πένθος in one line (17.470, οὔτ’ ἄχος … οὔτε τι πένθος) | "anguish" · "grief" | "anguish" · "grief" | "grief … grief" (the two Greek words must stay apart in one line), "pain" (reserved for ἄλγος), "distress" (reserved for ὀϊζύς); ἄχος keeps its shipped "grief" elsewhere, and πένθος stays "grief" at 17.489 |
| ὑπερφιάλως (17.481, adverb of ὑπερφίαλος "overweening") | "beyond measure" | "beyond measure" | "overweeningly" (it would sit beside the shipped "overweening young men" for ὑπερηνορεόντων at 17.482 and merge the two words), "arrogantly", "insolently" |
| ἐπουράνιος (17.484, θεὸς ἐπουράνιος) | "god of heaven" | "god of heaven" | "heavenly" (reserved for δῖος), "celestial", "god above" |
| οὐλόμενος (vocative οὐλόμεν’, 17.484; participle οὐλομένης, 17.474) | "ruinous one" · "ruinous" | "you ruinous man" · "ruinous" | "accursed", "cursed" (turned down at the table's φάρμακον οὐλόμενον); keeps "ruinous" as in the table's οὐλομένη γαστήρ "the ruinous belly" (15.344) |
| ἐπιστάτης (17.455, σῷ ἐπιστάτῃ; sense inferred from ἐφίστημι "stand by") | "dependant" | "dependant" | "attendant", "overseer", "suppliant" (each silently picks one guess); the note says the sense is a guess from the root |
| ἔπεχεν (17.410, imperfect of ἐπέχω "rest on") with λιπαρούς πόδας "sleek feet" | "was resting his sleek feet" | "rested his sleek feet" | "shining feet", "greased feet", "oiled feet" (λιπαρός is "sleek", as in the table's γῆρας λιπαρόν and λιπαρὰ κρήδεμνα) |
| εἰλαπινάζων (17.410) | "feasting" | "as he feasted" | "banqueting", "carousing" (adds a tone not in the word) |
| θρῆνυς (17.409, 17.462, 17.504; "footstool", shipped at 1.131 and 4.136 in the same sense) | "footstool" | "footstool" | "stool" (reserved for δίφρος), "bench", "footrest" |
| ἀργεννός (17.472, ἀργεννῇς ὀΐεσσιν) | "white" | "white" | "silvery", "gleaming" (reserved for γλαυκῶπις), "bright" |
| ὄλβιος (17.420, of the former rich man) | "prosperous" | "prosperous" | "blessed" (reserved for μάκαρ), "fortunate", "happy"; follows the shipped "prosperous" (17.354) |
| κακὰ βυσσοδομεύων (17.465 = 17.491) | "evils devising deep within" | "devising evil deep within" | "brooding evil" (shipped at 9.316 for the first-person line, but "devising" keeps the verb in both persons), "plotting ill"; kept identical at both occurrences, as the packet's repeated line requires, and follows the shipped "devising deep within" (8.272, 9.316) |
| ἀλαπάζω (17.424, ἀλάπαξε; no object stated) | "laid waste" | "brought ruin" | "sacked", "destroyed me" (supplies an object the Greek does not give) |
| ἐπίσχεσις · ἐλεητύς (17.451) | "restraint" · "pity" | "holding back" · "pity" | "scruple", "mercy", "sparing" (each narrows ἐλεητύς) |
| ἀχρημοσύνη (17.502) | "want of means" | "need" | "poverty", "want", "lack of money" |
| ἔμελλεν + future infinitive (17.412) | "was about" | "was about to" | "was destined to", "was going to" (colloquial) |
| καλά as adverb (17.460, 17.483 κάλ’) | "finely" | "unscathed" (17.460) · "well" (17.483) | "beautifully", "nobly"; the Greek word is the same, and `i` takes the sense each context needs |
| ὥς τις … ἐσσι προΐκτης (17.449, exclamatory ὥς) | "How … a beggar you are." | "What a … beggar you are." | "so bold a beggar" (reads as a comparison) |
| πολύπλαγκτος (17.425, ληϊστῆρσι πολυπλάγκτοισιν; πολυ- + πλάζω "drive astray") | "much-straying" | "far-roaming" | "much-wandering" ("wandering" is kept for ἀλάομαι / ἀλητεύω), "far-wandering", "wide-roving"; `l` follows the table's "straying" for πλάζω and `i` its "roaming" (πλαγκτοσύνη · πλάζω, 15.311), with "far-" for the intensive πολυ- |
